author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Rapper Macklemore said Monday that he was dropped from Ed Sheeran’s U.S. tour after making pro-Palestinian remarks during a Sept. 4 concert at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, Reuters reported.

The promoter for Sheeran’s Loop Tour told Rolling Stone that venue owners had notified organizers they would not allow Macklemore to perform on the remaining support dates. Sheeran had no immediate public comment.
Macklemore was scheduled to appear at eight of the 10 remaining shows, which are set to resume Sept. 19 in Philadelphia. He said he and Sheeran had difficult conversations during the past week.

Macklemore also said New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft helped rally some stadium owners against keeping him on the tour. Kraft said he felt responsible for speaking up when he believed a line had been crossed.

The dispute reflects the continuing conflict over how artists’ political statements are handled at commercial events. Macklemore denies being antisemitic and says criticism of Israel should not be equated with antisemitism.
dek: The rapper says the remaining support dates were canceled after venue owners objected to his political comments at a New Jersey concert.
headline: Macklemore dropped from Ed Sheeran’s U.S. tour after pro-Palestinian remarks
